title: Dangote Refinery Raises Petrol to ₦1,350/Litre Then Reverses Within Hours Under Public Pressure
detail: Africa's largest refinery, the Dangote Petroleum Refinery, raised its ex-depot petrol price by ₦75 to ₦1,350 per litre on May 6 — a second consecutive weekly hike — attributing the increase to global oil price pressures linked to Middle East conflict. Following immediate market and public backlash, the refinery reversed the increase the same day, holding at ₦1,275 per litre. The episode illustrated the volatility of domestic fuel pricing following subsidy removal and Nigeria's growing dependence on a single private refinery for domestic supply.

media.caption: Dangote Refinery raises and then reverses petrol price hike to ₦1,350/litre within hours on May 6

title: Naira Stabilizes Near ₦1,374/$ as IMF Revises Nigeria 2026 Growth Forecast to 4.1%
detail: The naira held near ₦1,374 per dollar at the official CBN window in early May 2026, with daily volatility dropping to approximately 0.5% from over 4% in 2024, signaling a period of relative stability following two years of historic devaluation. Following IMF/World Bank Spring Meetings, the IMF revised Nigeria's 2026 GDP growth forecast upward to 4.1%, citing the Tinubu government's ongoing reforms including banking sector recapitalization that raised ₦4.65 trillion. Nigeria simultaneously rejected a fresh IMF bailout, with officials insisting domestic reforms are on track.

media.caption: Naira stabilizes near ₦1,374/$ as Nigeria's economy shows signs of recovery; IMF lifts growth forecast
